insight.title: Light Takes Nine Hours to Circle the Largest Star
insight.subtitle: While light orbits the Earth in a fraction of a second, it takes nearly half a day to travel around a single supergiant star.
insight.notificationHook: Nine hours to orbit a single star

sections.text: At the speed of light, you could circle the Earth seven times in a single second. But if you flew around the hypergiant star Stephenson 2-18, the journey would take nine hours.
Located twenty thousand light-years away, this red supergiant is so massive that if placed at the center of our solar system, its outer edge would swallow the orbit of Saturn.
Our Sun, which could hold over a million Earths, is reduced to an invisible speck by comparison. It would take ten billion Suns to fill the volume of this single giant.
We live in a cosmos where even light can crawl.
